clue.text: Like sardines? Convulsion will follow being drunk

indicators.note: the convulsion piece comes after the drunk piece, so these words set the order

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a fit is a sudden convulsion or seizure

explanation.surface: A drunkard watches tinned sardines and feels a fit coming on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like sardines?' describes the state of being packed in a tin, which is what a tight fit is; the question mark admits the loose fit of noun to description.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardines are proverbially packed closely together in their tins, the very picture of something crammed in with no room.

clue.text: Possible answer to 10 12 9 11 in Scottish plant set fire to bank

indicators.note: the fire-setting word is placed inside the Scottish plant

parts.note: the thistle is the emblem of Scotland
lit is the past tense of light, to set fire to
a piggy bank is a child's money box, so bank suggests piggy

explanation.surface: A Scottish thistle is torched on a riverbank, with a nod to a fairy-tale question.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme's little pig is a possible reply to the song's question 'Who's afraid of the big bad wolf?'; 'in' places the lit word inside the thistle.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the pigs from the nursery rhyme could answer the question in the song title, being a creature that might fear the wolf.

clue.text: Round number entry — retire for night?

indicators.note: the number makes its entry into the bedtime phrase, so it goes inside

parts.note: go (to) bed means retire for the night; the question mark covers the shortened phrase
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A round-number moment arrives and someone wonders whether to turn in for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round number' looks like one phrase, but 'Round' is the definition and 'number' gives the Roman numeral L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something globed has been made into a sphere, so it is round in shape.

clue.text: A couple of beasts as in 10 12 9 11

parts.note: a nag is an old horse, one beast
a ram is a male sheep, the second beast

explanation.surface: Two animals turn up in a fairy-tale song title.
explanation.walkthrough: The long theme clue at 10 is itself a rearrangement of letters, which is what the definition points at.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue at 10 rearranges the letters of its fodder into the song title, so that answer is formed by this device.

clue.text: American company takes most of English city

indicators.note: only the greater part of the city's name is used, with the tail lopped off

parts.note: Manchester is a city in north-west England

explanation.surface: A US firm takes over most of a northern English city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comanche are a Native American people of the southern Great Plains.

clue.text: Sign in the rain on way round Suffolk town

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second, so it comes later

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the sign is placed inside the rainy word

parts.note: the wet is a name for rainy weather
a mark is a sign

explanation.surface: A sign spotted in the rain on a roundabout road near a Suffolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the sign inside the rain, and 'on' (below, in a down entry) sets that after the way and round. Stowmarket is a market town in Suffolk, an eastern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowmarket is a market town in the county of Suffolk in eastern England.

clue.text: Don't keep us in the dark planet

definitions.text: Don't keep us in the dark
definitions.meaning: an appeal to be told the news, said as two words
the Roman earth goddess, used as a name for the planet Earth

explanation.definitionFit: Tellus is the Latin name for the Earth goddess and so for our planet, and also reads as an urging to inform us.

clue.text: Guide finds river cold, piercing him from the East

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so everything is reversed

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

indicators.note: the cold letter goes through the middle of him, so it sits inside

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A guidebook locates a cold river that cuts into a man from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: C pierces HIM to make HCIM; NILE plus HCIM is NILEHCIM, and 'from the East' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Michelin Guide is the famous restaurant and travel guidebook published by the tyre company.

clue.text: See 10
Hobbit's flawed affair: how dog produced display of brute courage?

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are worked into a new form, as if produced afresh

parts.note: taken as written, the 's giving its S
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

annotation.spelling: WHO'S AFRAID OF THE BIG BAD WOLF

explanation.surface: A flawed Tolkien affair asks how a dog came to show bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flawed' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'produced' is the signal. The song from Disney's Three Little Pigs is sung defiantly by animals, hence brute courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The song is a show of defiance against a predator sung by the pigs, so it displays courage from animals, which are brutes.

clue.text: Former term for a river on island in the gulf

parts.note: a chasm is a gulf or abyss

explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is an old-fashioned word or expression no longer in everyday use.

clue.text: Miserable toerags may be cold

indicators.note: the wretched state of the louts tells us to rearrange their letters

explanation.surface: Wretched louts may well feel chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: TOERAGS is British slang for scoundrels; rearranged it gives the answer, and cold storage is the familiar pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold storage is the keeping of goods at low temperature, so this kind of keeping may be cold.

clue.text: Young female FBI agent now gone private employed by Nelson?

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI agent, so G stands for one
a lass is a young woman
a private eye is a detective, so an agent turned private suggests eye

explanation.surface: A young woman from the FBI has quit to become a private detective.
explanation.walkthrough: A female G-man is a G-LASS, and on going private she becomes an EYE. Admiral Nelson lost the sight of one eye; the question mark admits he did not actually wear an artificial one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson was blind in one eye, so an artificial eye is the sort of thing he might plausibly have used.

clue.text: Wanting a meal? Gregory's cooked his

indicators.note: cooked means messed with or prepared, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gregory has made his dinner, perhaps because he was hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling peckish means being slightly hungry, so wanting something to eat.

clue.text: Compact about raising single coil

indicators.note: the compact word wraps about the raised single

parts.note: solid means compact or dense

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upwards so it reads backwards

parts.note: one means single

explanation.surface: An agreement about lifting a single coil of wire.

explanation.definitionFit: A solenoid is a cylindrical coil of wire that acts as a magnet when current flows.

clue.text: Have visitors but don't serve?

clue.text: Begin to say you're opposed to the union?

parts.note: only the start of this phrase is used, the first part spoken

explanation.surface: Someone starts to declare that you are against the union.

explanation.definitionFit: The European Union is often simply called Europe, especially in British political debate.
